Imagine a team race, not where everyone runs at once, but like a relay! One runner goes first, and when they finish, they hand off to the next. That's how this week's special machine learning teams work. Each model passes its work to the next, helping solve tough problems together.

This process is called boosting. One simple model tries to solve a problem. Then, it sees where it made mistakes. The next model learns only from those mistakes, trying to fix them. This goes on, round after round, making the whole team much smarter at difficult tasks.

AdaBoost is a popular boosting method. When a model gets something wrong, AdaBoost makes those specific mistakes more important for the next model to learn. It's like giving extra homework to practice only the problems you missed. This helps the team focus better on tricky parts.

For your exams, remember to count how many models are trained in a grid search. Multiply the options for each setting, then multiply by the cross-validation folds! So, boosting builds sequential models, fixing mistakes. Stacking uses a referee model. These methods help us build truly powerful learning teams!
